manager_rule: Maintain a session-scoped boolean flag 'rule66_slot_yield_active' initialized to false. After each round R where ALL of the following hold simultaneously: (a) Rule 46 fires (n_stubs > 0 AND absorbed + trimmed_spurs == n_stubs AND kelvin_unrouted > 0), AND (b) excess_unconnected > 0 in round R (excess_unconnected = unconnected - 2*kelvin_unrouted - count of cables C with exactly one member in failing_reasons), AND (c) Rule 66 has at least one net in compiler_excess_unconnected_targets for R+1: apply the following slot-yield protocol. In round R+1: (1) identify the 'fully-absorbed nets' as every net that appeared in round R's directed stub summary 'nets' field AND whose stubs were entirely absorbed or trimmed (per-net absorbed_count + trimmed_count == stub_count_for_that_net); (2) suppress compiler stub injection for fully-absorbed nets in round R+1 ONLY — do NOT add them to compiler_excluded_nets and do NOT modify net_absorption_count; (3) allocate all freed stub slots in round R+1 first to mandatory Kelvin stubs (Rules 33/34/55 take absolute priority), then to nets in compiler_excess_unconnected_targets (Rule 66), then to any remaining compiler targets not in the suppressed set; (4) set rule66_slot_yield_active to true and log 'rule46_rule66_slot_yield' with: (a) round R, (b) suppressed net names and per-net absorbed+trimmed counts, (c) excess_unconnected count and net names in compiler_excess_unconnected_targets that receive freed slots, (d) kelvin_unrouted from round R, (e) confirmation suppression is round-R+1-only. In round R+2: restore all suppressed nets to normal compiler targeting unconditionally and reset rule66_slot_yield_active to false; log 'rule46_rule66_slot_yield_restored' with the restored net names. This rule is additive to Rules 46, 64, 65, and 66 and does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, kelvin_keepout_escalation_count, consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds, post_max_escalation_stall, or deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only. It is explicitly subordinate to Rules 33/34/55: mandatory Kelvin bypass always fires first regardless of slot-yield state. If Rule 64 or 65 also fires in round R for the same event, the slot-yield protocol applies additively to round R+1 alongside their deferral semantics; the R+2 bypass pass from Rule 64/65 proceeds normally in R+2. Rationale: at round 117, all 7 stubs for /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA were absorbed or trimmed, confirming FR connects those nets without guidance. Simultaneously, excess_unconnected=2 identifies 2 non-Kelvin ratlines on nets that Rule 66 has added to compiler_excess_unconnected_targets. Rule 66 schedules those nets for R+1 injection but does not prevent the 3 established nets from consuming all stub slots first, leaving the excess targets with zero guidance. The suppression costs nothing — the absorbed nets will be connected in R+1 without help, as demonstrated by their absorption in R — while giving Rule 66's excess targets dedicated slots they cannot otherwise compete for.
